# Leslie Moore

## Overview

- **Age:** Twenty-eight  <sub>[v2 c10 P49](../source/v02-c10.md#nw-v02-c10-p0049)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c1 P47](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0047)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v4 c38 P10](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0010)</sub>
- **Origin:** Four Winds (West farm)  <sub>[v2 c11 P15](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0015), [v2 c11 P28](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0028)</sub>
- **Role:** Former teacher, nurse-in-training  <sub>[v2 c11 P24](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0024), [v4 c38 P20](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0020)</sub>

## Appearance

Leslie is an exceptionally beautiful woman with sea-blue eyes and an abundance of living, burnished golden hair that reaches down to her feet. She has a high-bred face with a cream-white complexion, a rose-red mouth, and a magnificent, erect figure. Her appearance is often enhanced by a touch of crimson, such as a red ribbon or a geranium at her throat.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c6 P8](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0008), [v2 c11 P15](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0015), [v2 c23 P20](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0020), [v2 c28 P4](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0004), [v4 c5 P8](../source/v04-c05.md#nw-v04-c05-p0008), [v4 c12 P15](../source/v04-c12.md#nw-v04-c12-p0015), [v4 c23 P25](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0025)_

## Personality

Leslie possesses a proud, intense, and passionate nature that was long buried beneath a mantle of cold reserve and bitterness. Her early tragedies made her aloof and prone to brooding, occasionally harboring envy toward those who enjoyed the happiness denied to her. Once she opens her heart, she reveals a warm, witty, and deeply loyal soul capable of intense affection. She holds a strong, old-fashioned sense of duty and responsibility, enduring hardship without complaint rather than shirking her obligations.

_Sources: [v2 c11 P11](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0011), [v2 c11 P28](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0028), [v2 c21 P0](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0000), [v2 c21 P11](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0011), [v2 c21 P48](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0048), [v4 c21 P11](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0011), [v4 c25 P15](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0015), [v4 c30 P28](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0028)_

## History

Leslie's early life in Four Winds was marked by tragedy: her beloved brother Kenneth was killed in a wagon accident, and two years later her despondent father hanged himself. To save her widowed mother from being evicted from their farm, sixteen-year-old Leslie agreed to marry Dick Moore, whom she did not love. Shortly after her mother's death, Dick sailed away on the Four Sisters and disappeared. Captain Jim later found an amnesiac man in Havana whom he believed to be Dick Moore and brought him back to Four Winds. For twelve years, Leslie faithfully cared for the brain-damaged man, living in poverty and isolation in her ancestral homestead. Upon the arrival of Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe at Four Winds, Leslie initially felt a bitter envy toward Anne's happiness. However, she eventually confessed her feelings to Anne, breaking down her emotional barriers, and the two became devoted friends. When Gilbert suggested an operation that might restore Dick's memory, Leslie courageously agreed despite her dread of returning to a life with the man she had once loathed. The operation in Montreal succeeded in restoring the man's memory, revealing that he was actually Dick's cousin, George Moore, and that the real Dick Moore had died years earlier in Cuba. Finally freed from her tragic burden, Leslie returned to Four Winds. She fell in love with Owen Ford, a writer who had stayed at her house during the summer while writing his novel based on Captain Jim's life-book. They confessed their mutual love in Anne's garden, and Owen proposed to her.

## Background by volume

- Daughter of Frank West and Rose Elliott of Four Winds  <sub>[v2 c11 P15](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0015)</sub>
- Her younger brother Kenneth was tragically killed in a farm accident when she was twelve  <sub>[v2 c11 P16](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0016), [v2 c21 P39](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0039)</sub>
- Her father committed suicide when she was fourteen  <sub>[v2 c11 P20](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0020), [v2 c21 P44](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0044)</sub>
- Attended Queen's Academy and taught at Glen St. Mary school  <sub>[v2 c11 P24](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0024)</sub>
- Coerced into marrying Dick Moore at sixteen to prevent the foreclosure of her mother's farm  <sub>[v2 c11 P24](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0024), [v2 c21 P27](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0027)</sub>

## Quotes

> I can't tell you—don't ask me. I wouldn't mind your knowing—I wish you did know—but I can't tell you—I can't tell anyone. I've been such a fool, Anne—and oh, it hurts so terribly to be a fool. There's nothing so painful in the world.  <sub>[v4 c27 P11](../source/v04-c27.md#nw-v04-c27-p0011)</sub>

> If we are to be friends you must call me Leslie.  <sub>[v4 c10 P29](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0029)</sub>

> I had a house of dreams once—but it was a palace.  <sub>[v4 c10 P27](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0027)</sub>

> Anne, I never had anything to love since my mother died, except Dick's old dog—and it's so dreadful to have nothing to love—life is so EMPTY—and there's NOTHING worse than emptiness.  <sub>[v4 c21 P11](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0011)</sub>

> I ENVY Anne, and I'd envy her even if she had died! She was a mother for one beautiful day. I'd gladly give my life for THAT!  <sub>[v4 c19 P40](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0040)</sub>
